questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code validates booking requests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A request has checkIn in the past and an empty travelers list. What does the client receive?
choices: A 422 whose problems list contains the past-date message
A 400, because the annotation constraints fail first and BookingRules is never called
A 201, because the service decides whether to reject past dates
A 422 listing both the past-date problem and the missing travelers

questions.prompt: A request has checkIn 2030-05-10 and checkOut 2030-05-01 (all annotation constraints satisfied). Which describes what BookingRules does?
choices: It reports that checkOut must be after checkIn and does not compute a night count for that stay
It reports both the ordering problem and that the stay exceeds the night limit, because the negative count is compared as an absolute value
It throws an exception from ChronoUnit.DAYS.between
It reports only the night limit problem

questions.prompt: Why does BookingRules take a Clock instead of calling LocalDate.now() directly?
choices: So the current date used by the checks can be fixed in tests and is consistent with the application time zone configuration
Because bean validation requires a Clock bean
To avoid the cost of reading the system time on every request
